hints: Express cot²θ−tan²θ over the common denominator sin²θ cos²θ.
Factor the numerator cos⁴θ−sin⁴θ as a difference of squares.
Split the resulting 4cos2θ/sin²2θ into cot2θ times cosec2θ.
walkthrough:
Express the left-hand side in terms of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$:
$$\cot^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = \dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin^2\theta} - \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}$$

Factor the numerator as a difference of two squares:
$$\cos^4\theta - \sin^4\theta = (\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta)$$

Apply the Pythagorean identity $\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$ and the double-angle identity $\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = \cos(2\theta)$:
$$\text{Numerator} = \cos(2\theta) \times 1 = \cos(2\theta)$$

Use the double-angle formula $\sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta \implies \sin\theta\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\sin(2\theta)$ in the denominator:
$$\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\sin(2\theta)\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}\sin^2(2\theta)$$

hints: Replace the left side using part (a), then write sec2x as 1/cos2x.
Clear valid trigonometric denominators and reduce the equation to one in tan²2x.
Solve for both signs of tan2x while 0°<2x<180°.
Divide the admissible angles by 2 and give all solutions to the paper's degree accuracy.
walkthrough:
Use the identity from part (a) to substitute for $\cot^2 x - \tan^2 x$:
$$4\cot(2x)\operatorname{cosec}(2x) = 5\sec(2x)$$

Divide both sides by $5\cos^2(2x)$ to form an equation in $\tan^2(2x)$:
$$\dfrac{\sin^2(2x)}{\cos^2(2x)} = \dfrac{4}{5} \implies \tan^2(2x) = \dfrac{4}{5} = 0.8$$

Take the square root for both signs:
$$\tan(2x) = \pm\sqrt{0.8} \approx \pm 0.894427$$

Solve for $2x$ in the range $0^{\circ} < 2x < 180^{\circ}$ since $0^{\circ} < x < 90^{\circ}$:
$$\text{From } \tan(2x) = +0.894427: \quad 2x = \tan^{-1}(0.894427) \approx 41.8103^{\circ} \implies x = 20.905^{\circ} \approx 20.9^{\circ}$$
$$\text{From } \tan(2x) = -0.894427: \quad 2x = 180^{\circ} - 41.8103^{\circ} = 138.1897^{\circ} \implies x = 69.095^{\circ} \approx 69.1^{\circ}$$

State the final solutions correct to 1 decimal place:
$$x = 20.9^{\circ}, \quad 69.1^{\circ}$$
